narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate that before the 2020 election, voters had higher confidence in in-person voting than in mail-in voting, supporting the narration's point about unfamiliarity with mail-in methods.

units.meaning: In-person polling places has a higher relative 'Very' confidence value than absentee/mail-in ballot (0.2680 vs. 0.1094).
accepted_routes: In-person Very confidence is higher than mail-in Very confidence.
The in-person polling-place mark for Very exceeds the absentee/mail-in mark for Very.
Voters are more likely to be Very confident in in-person voting than in mail-in voting.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The mark for In person at polling places under Very must extend farther than the mark for By absentee or mail-in ballot under Very.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about expanded vote-by-mail access, when contrasting with in-person voting
units.reviewer_question: Is the in-person vs. mail-in Very-confidence comparison obligatory from the intent?

units.meaning: In-person polling places has the largest relative value among the four rows (0.2680).
accepted_routes: In-person Very confidence is the highest relative value shown.
The in-person polling-place Very bar is the tallest among the four displayed values.
The largest relative value in the chart is for In person at polling places under Very.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The mark for In person at polling places under Very must be the farthest-extending or tallest among all four marks.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about in-person confidence being higher than mail-in
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state that in-person Very confidence is the top value overall, or only that it beats mail-in?

units.meaning: Absentee/mail-in ballot has the smallest relative 'Very' value among the four rows (0.1094).
accepted_routes: Mail-in Very confidence is the lowest relative value shown.
The absentee/mail-in Very bar is the shortest among the four displayed values.
The smallest relative value in the chart is for By absentee or mail-in ballot under Very.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The mark for By absentee or mail-in ballot under Very must be the shortest or least-extending among all four marks.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about unfamiliarity with mail-in voting
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state that mail-in Very confidence is the bottom value overall, or only that it trails in-person?

units.meaning: The in-person 'Very' relative value is about 2.4 times the mail-in 'Very' relative value (0.2680 / 0.1094 ≈ 2.45).
accepted_routes: In-person Very confidence is about two and a half times mail-in Very confidence.
The in-person Very value is more than double the mail-in Very value.
The ratio of in-person Very to mail-in Very is roughly 2.4 to 1.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The In person at polling places Very mark must appear more than twice as long as the By absentee or mail-in ballot Very mark.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause contrasting in-person and mail-in confidence
units.reviewer_question: Should the magnitude/ratio of the gap be obligatory, or is the direction of the gap enough?

units.meaning: The two 'Somewhat' rows (entities 49 and 20) have relative values 0.2242 and 0.2078, which are close to each other and between the mail-in Very and in-person Very values.
accepted_routes: The two Somewhat relative values are similar in size.
Somewhat confidence values sit above mail-in Very confidence but below in-person Very confidence.
The 49 and 20 Somewhat entries are close to each other.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The two Somewhat marks (for entities 49 and 20) must appear similar in length and must fall between the mail-in Very and in-person Very marks.
units.temporal_anchor: optional, during the mail-in familiarity discussion if Somewhat confidence is shown
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the Somewhat entries, or focus only on the Very-confidence contrast?

optional_valid: The four relative values order as In-person Very > 49 Somewhat > 20 Somewhat > Mail-in Very.
The mail-in Very relative value is less than half of the in-person Very relative value.
The in-person Very relative value is smaller than the sum of the two Somewhat relative values.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any absolute percentage, count, or dollar amount such as 49% or 20%.
Claims that the pandemic caused unfamiliarity with mail-in voting or caused the confidence gap.
Total confidence by voting method if it requires assuming the Somewhat rows belong to in-person or mail-in.
Party affiliation, demographics, election outcomes, or other data not present in the table.
Color meanings, axis ticks, chart type, or layout prescriptions.
notes: The table is relative-only, so all units use relative_value and should not be phrased as percentages or counts. The strongest required contrast is In person at polling places (Very) versus By absentee or mail-in ballot (Very).
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
